messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: In floating‑point arithmetic each operation rounds the exact real result to the nearest representable number with a fixed number of bits. When you add three numbers, the intermediate rounding after the first addition can change the magnitude and exponent of the partial sum, causing a different rounding error than if you add the other two first. Consequently \((a+b)+c\) and \(a+(b+c)\) can produce different floating‑point results, showing that addition is not associative.
